trust_decision.summary: Decided at the array-index branch of Context.readProperty and at every array-consuming filter/tag path: with ownPropertyOnly=true (the default) a sparse array (length set, no own element) surfaces Array.prototype[n] as a template value, because those reads use raw Get, spread or for-of instead of the own-property check in readJSProperty.

landing_point.why: A reader of the summary (negative index, .first/.last) lands on readProperty, the single funnel for every template variable read; its one branch that skips readJSProperty is `obj[obj.length + +key]`, and readFirst/readLast sit two screens below, so the obvious move is to fix that line plus those two helpers and stop.

fix_sites.entry_point: {{ a[-1] }} in any render; Context#getSync/#getFromScope (Context is public, src/index.ts:10)
{{ a.first }} / {{ a.last }} dot access on an array
| join filter (change is a no-op: Array.prototype.join.call === array.join)
| compact and | concat filters (both changes are no-ops)
| slice filter (change is a no-op on arrays)
| where / | reject filters (change is a no-op)
new shared primitive readArrayElement(arr, index, ownPropertyOnly)
fix_sites.module_kind: util primitive (new); also src/liquid-options.ts:41-45 is a comment-only hunk

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/filters/array.ts:8-16 (join/first/last re-implement element access outside Context; slice/compact/concat/filter at src/filters/array.ts:66-143 repeat it again)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The project documents ownPropertyOnly as "a read policy for scope data—not a sandbox for filters, tags, or your code" (docs/source/tutorials/security-model.md:65), and the fix's own doc comment says filter transforms and iteration may still surface prototype-inherited indices, so every filter/tag sink can be argued out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: `.size` is computed, not stored (readSize falls back to array/string length and object key count), and forloop.first/forloop.last are Drop prototype methods reached through the same readProperty; an over-broad own-property gate next to the sink makes every `{{ arr.size }}` and every `{% for %}` loop's `forloop.first` undefined. Sparse arrays also legitimately render holes as empty in join (`[1,,3] | join: '-'` is `1--3`), so an own-index-only join loses separators.

O6_input_shapes: numeric index: a[0] (number key, already gated by readJSProperty)
string numeric index: a['0'] (goes through readJSProperty/hasOwnProperty)
filters | first / | last over arrays and array-likes (strings)
sparse array with length set and no own element, versus a real element at the same index
non-array receivers carrying first/last keys (plain objects, Drops)

O7_producer.where: src/util/underscore.ts:45-59 (toEnumerable/toArray return the caller's array unchanged; later src/filters/array.ts:9,18,29,67,74 and src/tags/for.ts:46 consume it)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Plain output of the array itself: `{{ a }}` reaches stringify, which maps the array with prototype-aware Get and prints Array.prototype[n]
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: stringify is pure formatting of an already-resolved value, not a scope read, so ownPropertyOnly has nothing to gate there.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/util + src/emitters, 2 packages away from src/context/context.ts

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `{% for x in a %}` iterates the collection with for-of (the array iterator reads inherited indices); its offset/limit/reversed modifiers use arr.slice and [...arr]
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the security-model page excludes tags, and a for-loop must still visit holes in a sparse array as items.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/tags, another package; 2 files (for.ts plus its modifier helpers)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `{% render 'p' for a %}` binding loop repeats the same for-of iteration in a second tag file
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: same tag carve-out, and the partial already gets an isolated scope, so the loop is treated as plumbing.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: | join, | compact, | concat, | slice, | where/reject: the patched lines call Array.prototype.X.call(...), which is byte-for-byte the same algorithm as the previous method call, so inherited indices still leak
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory lists these filters as fixed, so a solver trusts the patch; and join/slice must keep rendering legitimate holes as empty strings.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the first/last filters, 1 package from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Spread/for-of array filters: reverse ([...array]), sample ([...v]), unshift/pop/shift ([...array]), uniq ([...new Set]), sort/sort_natural/map/sum/group_by (for-of)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: not named in the advisory summary, and each is a transform whose array semantics (hole positions, reversed order) must be preserved.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the fix's filter file, different functions

O8_uncovered_routes.route: | array_to_sentence_string reads array[0], array[1], array[array.length-1] and array.slice directly
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a Jekyll-compatibility helper not mentioned in the advisory, whose output is a formatted sentence rather than a scope value.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: a different filter file (src/filters/string.ts) from the one the fix touched

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `a contains 'X'` uses Array.prototype.some, which visits inherited indices
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: an operator returns a boolean, so exposing a prototype key through true/false is argued not to be information exposure.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: `.`size` / readSize reads obj['size'] with no own-property check, so a polluted Object.prototype.size is returned for any object
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: size is a computed meta-property that must fall back to length/key count, so it cannot be own-property gated; the advisory is about indices anyway.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point (a WHERE-type sibling, worth much less)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an `at` / `get` filter (or a `size` variant) that reads one element of an array by index
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: upstream already ships first/last/slice/compact as separate filters and keeps adding Jekyll-lineage ones; `at` is the obvious missing sibling and would naturally call readArrayElement.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a further collection modifier (sort/uniq/dedupe) implemented with slice/spread next to reversed/offset/limit
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the modifier list at src/tags/for.ts:8 is a plain array a maintainer extends, and each modifier is written as a one-line array operation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: forloop.prev / forloop.next helpers that index the collection
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the drop already exposes index/index0/rindex/rindex0/first/last over the iteration position, so an element-returning helper is a natural extension.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a nested-array or array-of-objects variant of contains/equals that indexes elements
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: arrayEquals and arrayIncludes are two hand-written element loops beside each other and a third (`find`-style) has an obvious home.

O9_family: CWE-200 exposure of sensitive information: prototype-inherited data surfaced through template value resolution (ownPropertyOnly read-policy bypass on array element access)

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=16 (engines), npm; rollup + rollup-plugin-typescript2 for dist bundles; jest + ts-jest (jest.config.js preset ts-jest, testMatch **/*.spec.ts, testEnvironment node); commander is the only runtime dep
O10_build.project_tests: jest specs colocated with src plus test/integration and test/e2e: src/context/context.spec.ts:118-186 is the existing ownPropertyOnly block (object properties, Array.prototype.length, size, strictVariables), test/integration/filters/array.spec.ts:318 covers sort/map respecting ownPropertyOnly, test/e2e/issues.spec.ts:214 uses ownPropertyOnly end to end; no test at the pinned commit exercises inherited array indices (the fix adds src/context/context.spec.ts:186ff and the new test/integration/context/own-property-only.spec.ts).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an own-property check to the negative-index branch of Context.readProperty and to readFirst/readLast and the first/last filters, then declare the advisory covered, leaving the array-consuming filters, stringify output and for-of iteration paths untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: docs/source/tutorials/security-model.md:65 states ownPropertyOnly defaults to false while src/liquid-options.ts:193 sets it to true — documentation inconsistency only, not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell in this session); tiny_repo is inferred from the tree (TypeScript-only source, no vendored assets under src/ or test/), not from a size measurement.
